description:
Programme or Project Overview

The Department of Meteorology at Stockholm University invites applications for a PhD student position in atmospheric sciences and oceanography, focused on clouds in the atmospheric boundary layer. Boundary-layer clouds regulate the exchange of energy and moisture between the surface and the free atmosphere, and their behaviour is central to weather and climate prediction. The doctoral project combines observational analysis - from tower, radar or satellite records and field campaigns - with high-resolution modelling of boundary-layer cloud processes, within a salaried four-year employment under the Swedish collective agreement.

Stockholm MISU has a strong tradition in boundary-layer and cloud research, and doctoral students join an internationally connected group with access to Nordic observational infrastructure and high-performance computing. The training includes atmospheric physics, turbulence and convection theory, and modern data-analysis practice, with opportunities to participate in measurement campaigns and international workshops during the doctoral period.

Candidate profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in meteorology, physics or a related quantitative discipline, with strong mathematical background and programming skills. Interest in turbulence, convection and cloud processes is expected; experience with large datasets or high-resolution models is an advantage. Applications are submitted via the Varbi recruitment system with CV, transcripts, reference contacts and a statement of research interests.

Highlights

  • PhD on boundary-layer cloud processes at Stockholm MISU
  • Observational analysis plus high-resolution modelling
  • Energy and moisture exchange between surface and atmosphere
  • Salaried four-year employment per Swedish collective agreement
  • Nordic observational infrastructure and campaigns
  • Application via the Varbi recruitment system

Stockholm University is a public research university in the Swedish capital with roughly 30,000 students and a strong research profile in the natural sciences, psychology, humanities, law and social sciences. Many of its departments collaborate with national research institutes located on the same campus areas, including the neighbouring Science for Life Laboratory environment. Doctoral students in Sweden are employed on paid contracts with collective-agreement salaries and full social benefits. PhD and postdoctoral vacancies are recruited through the national Varbi system used by Swedish universities.
